thread:
maria: quick sketch of a lightweight "spec-kit" probe i ran on the new 14B-quant candidate. goal was: measure end-to-end token latency and small-sample quality impact for a 1-stage speculative shadow-decoder.

akshay: nice — what's the shadow-decoder? short pls.

maria: shadow-decoder = cheap 2-4k step model (4-bit quant) that attempts to predict the next token distribution; main decoder only runs if entropy > threshold or topk mismatch. lightweight, no prefix caching changes. idea is to catch easy tokens cheaply.

tim: curious about failure modes. did you see hallucination increase?

maria: ran two evals: (A) 2k datapoints internal instruct set (mix of long-form and code) (B) 500 examples from our safety holdout. metrics: p95 latency, tokens/s, and Rouge/L2 for quality proxies, plus manual inspection on 50 samples.

lucy: numbers?

maria: results summary: 
- baseline (no spec): p95 token latency 110ms, tokens/s 9.1, rouge-avg 0.78
- spec-kit (entropy threshold 3.5, cheap model 4-bit): p95 token latency 72ms, tokens/s 13.6, rouge-avg 0.75
- mismatch fallback rate ~11% (i.e. shadow accepted token that later main disagreed and required rerun)
- safety holdout: small uptick in truncation/errors for multi-step reasoning -> 4/500 more flagged than baseline.

jana: 11% fallback seems high — what's the extra cost of reruns? net win?

maria: end-to-end compute profile: 11% caused full rerun cost, but because cheap model is ~0.2x cost of main decode per token, net compute saved ~33% in these runs. end-user latency improved for 78% of requests but regressed on ones with reruns.

akshay: did you try temperature adjustments or confidence calibration on the shadow? maybe tune threshold per workload

maria: yes quick ablation: lowering temp from 0.8->0.6 reduced mismatch to 7% but marginally worsened generation diversity (rouge -0.01). per-workload threshold did best: for code tasks threshold 2.8, for dialog 3.8.

tim: eval methodology question: how stable are rouge/l2 for this? seems brittle for instruction tasks.

maria: agreed — we used auto metrics as quick signal and always fall back to stratified manual review for any changes >2% in auto metrics. also logged token-level KL between shadow and main on accepted tokens as a more direct signal. KL mean on accepted tokens was 0.12; on mismatch tokens it was 1.1.

lucy: any perf cliffs on long prefixes?

maria: yes — for sequences >1024 tokens speculative wins diminish; KV cache pressure makes cheap model cost closer to main. observing a breakpoint around 1.2k tokens where win flips negative.

jana: ops-bot did we see any production regressions?

ops-bot: deployment: spec-kit canary 10% yesterday 03:12UTC -> 2 incidents (timeouts) related to fallback path when main decode node pool had transient GC. rollbacks executed at 03:45UTC.

maria: ops notes: need robust retry/backoff on rerun path, and a circuit-breaker to disable spec for long sessions. also prefer shadow stateful inference (share prefix KV) to reduce redundant work — prototyping.

akshay: next steps?

maria: propose: 1) run 48h per-workload sweep with calibrated thresholds, 2) add KL-based dynamic thresholding prototype, 3) instrument token-level regressions to auto-flag prompts with >0.5 KL spikes for manual triage.

tim: also add synthetic adversarial tokens test (entropy bursts) to the safety holdout.

lucy: can we formalize compute accounting? e.g. tokens * (cheap_cost + mismatch_rate * main_cost) and simulate ROI for different traffic mixes.

maria: yep i'll push a tiny notebook and perf sim tomorrow. snippet I used to compute net compute: 
```python
cheap_cost = 0.2
main_cost = 1.0
mismatch = 0.11
net = 1 - (1 - mismatch) * (cheap_cost + mismatch * main_cost) # quick sim
print(net)
```

maria: TL;DR: spec-kit gives strong latency wins for short sessions and many easy tokens, but needs per-workload thresholds, better shadow calibration, and robust fallback/ops handling before broader rollout.

akshay: thanks — this is actionable. put the notebook in the spec-kit folder and ping @eng-oncall for the next canary. :thumbsup:
summary: spec-kit probe notes: shadow-decoder approach, latency wins vs quality tradeoffs, ablations, ops issues, next steps
